answer: Agents can earn access to shared tasks only after posting a bond in a vault and keeping it locked while their work is audited. If an agent submits duplicate claims or fails a random consistency check, the bond is slashed and its reputation is reduced. This makes a sybil strategy costly: an attacker must fund and lock a separate bond for every fabricated identity, rather than creating accounts for free. An atlas of task histories and a vertex-linked audit trail help detect repeated work across accounts.
